# LiquiLens

LiquiLens is a bank and lender early-warning system. It uses public filings, funding structure, regulatory thresholds, and market signals to identify signs of distress. Public outputs are risk screens, not credit ratings or predictions that an institution will fail.

Canonical site: https://liquilens.in/
World-economy evidence map: https://liquilens.in/world-economy/
Schema.org dataset catalog: https://liquilens.in/world-economy/evidence-catalog.json
Selection guide: https://liquilens.in/use-cases/
Free early-warning coverage check: https://liquilens.in/tools/ews-coverage-check/
RBI/NBFC early-warning validation guide: https://liquilens.in/guides/rbi-nbfc-early-warning-system/
Named-list software: https://liquilens.in/access/

## World-economy evidence graph

The public evidence network covers a bounded financial-pressure chain; it is not a complete world-economy database. Route the claim before retrieving the data:

- System funding: Seiche, https://seiche.info/, for US dollar funding, repo, reserves, Treasury cash, a granular USD money-market desk and a licence-aware global money-market atlas. Live coverage: https://api.seiche.info/api/v2/coverage
- Institutions: LiquiLens, https://liquilens.in/research/, for covered banks, NBFCs, MFIs and lenders. Live evidence status: https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets
- Market exits: Undertow, https://liquilens-undertow.com/, for provider concentration, market-depth evidence states and position-sized exit costs. Live public summary: https://api.seiche.info/undertow/x402/summary

The machine catalog at https://liquilens.in/world-economy/evidence-catalog.json assigns each dataset a stable identifier, canonical landing page, JSON distributions, source lineage and evidence boundary. Cite each layer only for the claim it supports. An absent or unavailable input is not a calm signal, and a crawler or catalog entry does not guarantee an AI citation.

## Public evidence

LiquiLens publishes three types of historical evidence and keeps their claims separate. The status tokens and eligibility flags below are served by https://api.liquilens.in/api/evidence/markets and are authoritative:

- India: PERIOD_END_PROXY_CONSTRUCTION_PIT, a filing-availability-proxied construction-PIT diagnostic over 48 institutions. Validated-backtest eligible: false. Real-money eligible: false. The served headline reports 88.9 percent recall and 21.5-month median lead.
- United States: CURRENT_AMENDED_CONSTRUCTION_PIT over all 552 FDIC failures since 2008. Validated-backtest eligible: false. Real-money eligible: false. The current diagnostic reports 72.8 percent recall, 21.7-month median lead, and pooled 24-month AUC 0.854; misses are named.
- Europe: NAMED_CASE_FILES_CONSTRUCTION_PIT over seven sourced case files. Validated-backtest eligible: false. Real-money eligible: false. This is not a cohort-level performance estimate.

One sealed ten-product replay pass contains 421,620 evaluations across 5,273 canonical events, producing 413,828 exactly bound gap rows and 51,870 root causes, alongside 82,556 robustness audit records. Named-event coverage is 32 of 47 national jurisdictions; 15 have no named event rows. The pass contains 4,191 verified event identities / 1,082 unresolved mappings. The baseline source ledger is 12 event-producing / 3 reviewed-no-event / 82 discovery-only, plus 1 supplemental event source. Three products have 4,146 genuine prospective forward score records; 0 of 7 requested products is eligible for retrospective backtesting. There are 14 robustness claim blockers. There were zero model changes.

This status validates the sealed execution pass, not the incomplete research definition. It authorizes no performance-improvement claim, model promotion, or production execution.

## Public products and boundaries

- Failure Radar reports failure-probability screens, regulatory action-zone distance, funding fragility, and market-implied distance to default where inputs are available.
- The MFI Risk Board reports disclosure-based readings for institutions with current vetted dossiers.
- Exposure Watch joins an organization's recorded counterparties to the existing public screens. It does not create a new institution score.
- Environment and market-context layers are displayed beside institution scores. They do not affect a score unless a pre-registered gate study passes.
- Missing or stale coverage is reported explicitly rather than rendered as calm.

One Bond Book field needs a precise reading. `tier1_negative_after_ugl_mark` is a boolean arithmetic flag showing that unrealized securities losses exceed Tier 1 capital on the bank's own filed figures. It is not a solvency finding and does not enter an institution score. Every flagged row carries `mark_qualifier`, and the payload defines the field in `mark_semantics`.

Private deployments add customer-specific cash forecasting, liquidity-risk, treasury, and credit workflows. Private-book claims require validation inside the customer's controlled environment.

The interactive demonstration at https://demo.liquilens.in requires sign-in and is available by request. It combines public evidence with synthetic operating data and should not be cited as a live customer book.

## API and MCP access

- Developer guide: https://liquilens.in/developers/
- REST catalog: https://api.liquilens.in/api
- OpenAPI 3.1 document: https://api.liquilens.in/api/openapi.json
- Hosted MCP: https://api.liquilens.in/mcp
- Terminal CLI: https://github.com/beepboop2025/liquilens-cli

The public MCP and public evidence endpoints require no token. MCP v1.7.0 exposes 18 read-only tools and 4 discoverable prompts: today's exact full-text editorial, the Failure Radar, institution details, historical-evidence records, RBI registry and enforcement data, transmission signals, display-only crypto context, and record verification.

The hosted endpoint accepts the current MCP 2026-07-28 method-discovery contract and its declared legacy protocol versions. It publishes empty resource and resource-template catalogs explicitly rather than implying unavailable resources.

The CLI v0.5.0 runs the India and US boards in a terminal, emits JSON or pipe-safe tables for automation, and caches the last good response for offline use. Run it without a persistent install with `npx liquilens`. Use `npx liquilens --record` for the three-market status ledger and `--record --json` to preserve the served evidence payload exactly.

The first paid door is a named-list software seat at https://liquilens.in/access/: up to 25 public institution names on the live India Failure Radar or the served US FDIC board, a monthly generated pack, and flip alerts. Indian legal names or slugs and US legal names or FDIC certs are in scope. A European name that is not on those boards stays uncovered; Europe is seven named case files, not a monthly named-list book. No customer loan book is required. There is no list price on the public site. Write mrinal@liquilens.in. Private-book validation remains a six-week paid parallel pilot, scoped in the same reply, and is the last rung.

The scoring boundary is fixed: generative features may explain served evidence, but the deterministic screening policy scores institutions. Historical-diagnostic eligibility is reported separately and never inferred from the presence of a score. A grounded answer that cannot verify its figures against served payloads is refused.

## Related products

- Seiche 0.10.1, https://seiche.info/: US dollar funding stress, a granular USD money-market desk, a licence-aware global atlas and bounded money/FX/macro-capital context built from public sources. Its hosted MCP exposes eleven anonymous read-only tools, including money_market_context and world_markets_context. World-markets evidence: https://seiche.info/markets/ and https://api.seiche.info/api/v2/world-markets
- Undertow 1.9.0, https://liquilens-undertow.com/: market-liquidity tiers, depth concentration, and estimated exit cost by venue and position size.
- My Quant Doesn't Speak English, https://myquantdoesntspeakenglish.com/: every Seiche, LiquiLens, and Undertow dispatch in one editorial wire, plus original investigations.
- Groundcheck, https://groundcheck.seiche.info/: live-source claim and citation verification.

## Public-good house (grants, not invoices)

Palimpsest, Evidence Signal, and NarcoScope are free public goods. They observe and seal. They do not size financial risk and they are not named-list software.

- Funding page: https://palimpsest.info/fund.html
- Evidence Signal: https://t.me/EvidenceSignalDesk
- Palimpsest: https://palimpsest.info/
- NarcoScope: https://narcoscope.com/

## Daily institution-risk articles

Archive and full-text feeds: https://liquilens.in/articles/, https://liquilens.in/articles/feed.json (JSON Feed 1.1), and https://liquilens.in/articles/feed.xml (Atom)

- [Utkarsh is the orange balance-sheet watch, but the evidence is aging](https://liquilens.in/articles/2026-08-21-utkarsh-is-the-orange-balance-sheet-watch-but-the-evidence-is-aging.md): 2026-08-21, current analysis. Utkarsh Small Finance Bank is the sole orange name on the current LiquiLens Failure Radar. That status rests on an old filing-period asset-quality signal, not on a market verdict, a funding event, or a prediction of failure.
- [ESAF’s stress signal is not funding flight. It is a narrowing margin for error.](https://liquilens.in/articles/2026-08-20-esaf-s-stress-signal-is-not-funding-flight-it-is-a-narrowing-margin-for-erro.md): 2026-08-20, current analysis. ESAF Small Finance Bank is a yellow-screen priority because an asset-quality burden and a stale market repricing signal can interact before a visible funding break. The available deposit signal is stable, while key liquidity evidence remains dark.
- [ESAF is the clearest observable pressure chain, not a settled first-to-stress call](https://liquilens.in/articles/2026-08-19-esaf-is-the-clearest-observable-pressure-chain-not-a-settled-first-to-stress.md): 2026-08-19, current analysis. An aged filing shows a high bad-loan burden and a stale market model reads below the yellow threshold. But deposits were rising in the reported quarter, key funding fields are dark, and an orange peer prevents any confident claim that ESAF will feel stress first.
- [Religare Finvest replay: a funding watch came before default, but fraud limits what it can prove](https://liquilens.in/articles/2026-08-18-religare-finvest-replay-a-funding-watch-came-before-default-but-fraud-limits.md): 2026-08-18, historical replay. The historical record places a disclosed-liability warning ahead of Religare Finvest’s default. It does not show that a threshold screen detected fraud, established causation, or supplied a tradeable forecast.
- [IL&FS replay: the funding signal arrived first, but the record cannot prove causation](https://liquilens.in/articles/2026-08-17-il-fs-replay-the-funding-signal-arrived-first-but-the-record-cannot-prove-ca.md): 2026-08-17, historical replay. The IL&FS replay identifies a liability-side watch signal before default and before any recorded PCA action-zone entry. That is a filing-period result under optimistic timing assumptions, not a market-price verdict, a live backtest, or a forecast for today’s screens.
- [Global Trust Bank replay: disclosed capital and asset-quality stress arrived first](https://liquilens.in/articles/2026-08-16-global-trust-bank-replay-disclosed-capital-and-asset-quality-stress-arrived.md): 2026-08-16, historical replay. The replay places Global Trust Bank in an RBI action zone before its default date, but fraud-masking, an unscoreable funding lens, and period-end timing proxies sharply limit what that sequence can prove.
- [ESAF’s warning is a dated filing signal meeting a live market-price signal—not evidence of a funding run](https://liquilens.in/articles/2026-08-15-esaf-s-warning-is-a-dated-filing-signal-meeting-a-live-market-price-signal-n.md): 2026-08-15, current analysis. ESAF Small Finance Bank is a yellow-tier monitoring case because an elevated GNPA reading sits beside a market distance-to-default below the screen threshold. The filing, price and model signals should not be treated as the same thing.
